name: NAM Amp
purpose: Neural capture of a real guitar amp, pedal or bass rig, played through Neural Amp Modeler, with a noise gate and bass/mid/treble tone stack around it.

params.name: Input level
params.ai_hint: Drive into the capture. Raise for more gain and breakup, lower for cleaner tones. Check the input meter before pushing it.

params.name: Noise gate
params.ai_hint: Gate threshold. -100 is off. Use -70 to -55 for high-gain tones; keep it low for clean playing so notes decay naturally.

params.name: Bass
params.ai_hint: 5 is flat. Lower to tighten a muddy low end.

params.name: Mid
params.ai_hint: 5 is flat. Lower for scooped metal tones, raise for cut.

params.name: Treble
params.ai_hint: 5 is flat. Raise for presence, lower to tame fizz.

params.name: Output level
params.ai_hint: Trim after the capture. Output is already loudness-matched when normalise is on.

params.name: Normalise output
params.ai_hint: Keep on so swapping captures does not change the volume.

notes: Parameters are written by hand: they drive Neural Amp Modeler Core (the capture), the NAM plugin's tone stack and AudioDSPTools' noise gate, not plugin ports.
The capture itself is a .nam file chosen from the user's library (or TONE3000); the AI picks it by file name through the slot's 'file' field and never invents one.
With no capture loaded the module passes audio through unchanged.
Captures are mono; stereo input is summed to mono and the result is sent to both channels.

CPU: Neural Amp Modeler Core is the heaviest module. The A2 example capture used 15% of one core and the standard WaveNet example 31% at 48 kHz on Plugsalot's 2-core build machine (plugin/tests/TestMain.cpp); 8 points is typical for a light capture and heavy captures cost more (capped at 10).
